verdict:
The register WAS incomplete, in the exact way the brief predicted: every miss was a name-or-index contract that fails silently. Seven of them were proven undetected — I built seven realistic corruptions (fixtures G1-G7) that both gates passed with violations=0 and exit 0 before any change. Root cause of five of the seven: the survey and the register only ever scanned module JS. Name lookups also live inside pack content (Macro.command), and the crit-parse lockstep had two more branches with a different splitter and different fixed indices.

GATE PROOF (harness: 4-常用脚本/qa/gate_fixtures/run_gates.py, reproducible from the project dir).
Day-one, real project, compendium/cn empty: traps checked=0 violations=0 exit=0; crit checked=8 violations=0 exit=0. Both still exit 0 after all changes.
Specificity — fixture GOOD, a full rule-abiding cn translation of all three packs (all 144 character-branch + 58 other-branch crit rows translated in lockstep, all 60 actor rTables/cTables refs written out): traps exit=0 checked=195 viol=0; crit exit=0 checked=190 viol=0.
Sensitivity — 23 single-injection mutants, each exits 1 on the gate that owns its rule and 0 on the other. Name-trap side M1-M12: FROZEN_TRANSLATED x8 (adventure name, welcome journal, scene, rolltable, folder, PACK MULE, the 'Critical Injuries' prefix filter, unparseable file), EXACT_MISMATCH x2, TABLE_REF_DANGLING x3. Crit side C1-C10: LANG_BAD, SPLIT_SHAPE (full-width colon; lost ': '), CELL_MISMATCH (FATAL, TIME LIMIT, Permanent, and EN DASH U+2013 -> ASCII hyphen), SHIFT_TRANSLATED, ROLL_SHAPE. Only M13 (unparseable JSON) trips both, deliberately.
Gap closure — all 7 previously-invisible corruptions now fail: G1/G2/G5/G6 on the traps gate, G3/G4/G7 on the crit gate, with GOOD still clean.
